sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year from $129,025 million in FY2017 to $303,154 million in FY2026 [F1][F10][F203].
The shape is a steady climb with two step changes: growth of 17.5% in FY2021 and 15.8% in FY2022, against 5.0% in FY2024 [D189][D238][D336].
FY2021's jump came from a 16% comparable sales increase, with non-foods and e-commerce particularly strong [P56].
FY2022's increase was driven by 14% comparable sales, led by gasoline, business centers and travel, with inflation also cited [P42].
Growth re-accelerated to 10.1% in FY2026, the fastest since FY2022, on 8% comparable sales and 25 net new warehouses [D434][P14].
The US segment supplied 72.5% of FY2026 revenue and 7.2pp of growth, with Other International adding 1.6pp [D670][D672][D679].
By product, Food and Sundries contributed 2.6pp and Warehouse ancillary 3.7pp in FY2026, the latter on 19.9% growth [D560][D601][D600].
Membership fees grew 11.0% to $5,907 million on new sign-ups, fee increases and Executive upgrades [D664][S78][P13].
Operating income grew 12.5% against revenue growth of 10.1%, an incremental margin of 4.7% [D435][D434][D457].
Diluted EPS grew 14.0% against net income growth of 13.9%, as the diluted share count was essentially flat at 444.4 million [D438][D436][X100].
Operating margin reached 3.9% in FY2026, the window high, against a 3.4% median and a 3.1% low in FY2019 [F32][D691][D692][D690].
The FY2026 margin rose 0.1pp, with SG&A adding 0.1pp and cost of revenue flat [D447][D460][D459].
SG&A fell 10 basis points as a share of sales, though it rose one basis point excluding gasoline price inflation, and currency added $126 million [P9].
Gross margin fell three basis points, with IEEPA tariff refunds adding three basis points and sales mix shifting toward ancillary businesses [P12].
Net margin of 3.0% sits 0.8pp below operating margin, reflecting interest and tax, and ranks at the 17th percentile against a 3.5% retail peer median [F52][D732][D711][D712].
Operating cash flow of $15,817 million was 1.71x net income, above the 1.75x window median's neighbourhood and well above the 1.26x low [F82][D421][D722][D721].
The FY2026 increase was primarily due to higher operating income and a reduced net investment in merchandise inventories from faster turns and better supplier terms [P6].
Free cash flow of $9,382 million was 1.02x net income and 3.1% of revenue, against a 2.8% window median [F102][D422][D418][D698].
Capex of $6,435 million was 2.1% of revenue and 2.41x D&A, the highest ratio in the window [F92][D417][D423].
Net cash reached $15,139 million, or 5.0% of revenue, up from $9,496 million, ranking at the 100th percentile against a peer median of -18.3% (n=4) [D427][D428][D378][D733][D734].
Total debt of $6,162 million includes $2,248 million current, while long-term debt fell 31.5% to $3,914 million [D426][X160][F192][D445].
Buybacks and dividends of $3,306 million were 35.2% of free cash flow, with $848 million of repurchases leaving $1,115 million under the authorization [D429][D430][X110][P3].
The diluted share count fell 0.1% in FY2026, so per-share growth tracked net income growth rather than exceeding it [D452][D438][D436].
Operating margin of 3.9% is the window high but only the 17th percentile against a 5.0% retail peer median, so the model runs on volume, not margin [F32][D709][D710].
Capex has grown 11.1% a year against 10.0% revenue growth, lifting capex to 2.41x D&A, which pressures free cash flow if warehouse returns disappoint [F209][F203][D423].
Free cash flow margin sits at the 50th percentile against a 4.2% peer median, below the FY2020 window high of 3.6% [D713][D714][D697].
The pack lists no red-flag candidates, so these are drawn from the cited metrics rather than an R series.
Operating margin: a print above the FY2026 high of 3.9% would confirm the margin trend, while a fall back to the 3.4% median would reverse it; watch the FY2027 10-K [F32][D691][D692].

Free cash flow to net income: holding at or above the 0.99x window median would confirm cash quality, while a drop toward the 0.60x low would flag capex or working-capital strain; watch the FY2027 cash flow statement [D701][D699].
Membership fee growth: staying above the 11.0% FY2026 rate would confirm the fee engine, while a fall toward the 5.4% FY2024 rate would signal renewal pressure; watch the FY2027 10-K [D664][D658].
